contour lines, dot grids, and rhythmic notation

claim_evidence.anchor: thirty-two melody attacks, four in every bar
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: 8 authored bars x 4 original quarter-note melody events = 32 attacks; source only provides dictation pedagogy.

claim_evidence.anchor: A note G in the bass could support G major
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Harmonic inference limitation from authored root-only example; 2013 paper motivates ambiguity but not this progression.

claim_evidence.anchor: The third bar is an especially useful question
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original G7 bar over G3 with melody D4 F4 G4 B4; composer authored data.

claim_evidence.anchor: A pitched sound's harmonics often create several horizontal bands
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Smith STFT/Time-Frequency Displays and example spectra; spectrum is a representation of partials.

claim_evidence.anchor: Choose a very long window and you may distinguish close steady frequencies better
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Smith online book STFT and spectrum-analysis windows; time/frequency trade-off.

citation_policy: Claim anchors are exact spoken substrings. A source ID and locator report what a source does and does not establish. Original calculations/scores remain author-derived, not misattributed primary findings. The URL/anchor validator cannot independently prove support.
